newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil steady, U.S. fall seen hitting prices.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil steady, U.S. fall seen hitting prices.

text.p: NWE low sulphur fuel oil prices appeared steady on Wednesday but cheap U.S. supplies and falling Brent crude futures pointed to a dip in values, traders said.
Activity was thin in both low sulphur barge and cargo markets and traders were unwilling to target physical prices.

A buyer was heard to have picked up two low sulphur cargoes in NWE on Tuesday in a bid to cover short positions, possibly into Portugal. Prices were heard at 98.50 and 94 FOB with talk of higher offer for small pieces.
Low sulphur fuel oil in the U.S. Gulf fell sharply to around $13.25 a barrel.
Traders reckoned that price, with freight, could bring cargoes to Europe at around $100 a tonne CIF Med.
Buyers in Italy said they had indications of prices dropping towards that level but had not so far seen specific offers far below $105.
Brent crude futures for the future month fell 29 cents to $19.21 at 1830gmt, continuing their bearish trend.

Little business was done in high sulphur cargoes or barges. Cargoes were notionally steady at $85 cif. Barges were offered early in the day at $92 fob ARA but prices then eased with deals done at $90.
